result: {"findings": [{"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 50, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "The example unwinds past live completions: `cq` and `mails` die on a stack frame the loops still point into", "body": "`cq` and `mails` are locals of the `go` coroutine. The teardown cancels the two drivers and the feeder, but nothing ever calls `cq.close()` / `cq.cancelAll(...)` / drain. A driver that re-submits a mail (`try cq.submit(c)`) and is then canceled leaves that `ev.Async` armed in `cq.pending`; the feeder's last `m.notify()` pass can also leave completions in flight on the loops. `go` then returns, the coroutine stack goes back to the stack pool and is reused, and `rt.deinit()` tears the loops down. Each of those completions still carries `c.group.owner == &cq` and `owner_callback == &ownerCallback`, so the loop calls `ownerCallback`, which locks `cq.mutex`, splices `pending`/`completed`, and does a `fetchAdd` on `cq.signal` -- all writes into a dead, possibly reused frame. `examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig:80-84` documents exactly this hazard and guards its early-return path with `errdefer { cq.close(); cq.cancelAll(.keep); while (cq.next()) |_| {} }`. Add the equivalent `defer` here (`.discard` is correct: the mails live in this frame). Consequence: a memory-corrupting teardown in the very example that is supposed to prove the queue's misuse detection, and a non-zero exit from an unrelated crash that the death-test oracle would read as success."}, {"file": "build.zig", "line": 81, "severity": "major", "category": "tests", "title": "The new death test is only built, never run: no harness exists in the repo", "body": "`examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig:6-9` states the contract \"a harness runs it and checks for a NON-zero exit. Exit 0 means the misuse was silently accepted\". The only thing this change adds is a row in the `examples` table, and `examples_step` merely `addInstallArtifact`s each executable -- it never runs one. `zig build test` does not touch examples at all. So the regression guard for the single-driver rule is a manual step that nothing enforces: the claims protocol can regress to silent acceptance and every build step still passes. The rule needs a step that executes the binary and asserts the abort (a `b.addRunArtifact` with an expected non-zero termination, or an equivalent unit test that provokes the second registration), not an example nobody launches."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 11, "severity": "major", "category": "tests", "title": "Exit-code-only oracle cannot distinguish the documented panic from any other abort", "body": "The header names a specific expected outcome -- the panic text `CompletionQueue: selected from two tasks; one task must drive the queue` (`src/completion_queue.zig:429`) -- but then specifies the check as \"a NON-zero exit\". Every other abort produces the same verdict: the pre-claims `getResult` assert at `src/completion_queue.zig:382`, which the same header names as the old far-from-the-cause symptom; a use-after-free crash from the missing queue teardown; and an ordinary error return, because `try handle.join()` in `main` propagates any error out of `go` (a failed `runtime.spawn`, a canceled `runtime.sleep`) and Zig exits non-zero for it. So the probe reports PASS for the exact failure it was written to distinguish. The oracle must match the panic message on stderr, not just the exit status."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 1475, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "\"close claims the drained state to a parked select\" can pass without the driver ever parking", "body": "The test's only synchronization is a fixed 20 ms `ev.Timer` before `cq.close()`, and nothing asserts that the driver actually reached `asyncWait` and installed `self.reg`. If the spawned task has not registered yet (a loaded machine, a slow spawn, a scheduler that has not run it), `close()` finds `self.reg == null`, takes the `signal.fetchAdd` + `Futex.wake` path instead, and the driver's later `asyncWait` returns through the ready fast path at `src/completion_queue.zig:398` with `drained = true`. The assertion `expectError(error.Closed, result.io)` still holds, so the test goes green while the `claimToRegistered` path it is named for was never executed. Make the registration observable before closing -- for example spin on a state the queue exposes, or have the test fail if the close did not take the claim branch -- so that a regression in the claim path cannot hide behind a timing slip."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 69, "severity": "trivial", "category": "style", "title": "Uses the deprecated `Runtime.sleep` method instead of `zio.sleep`", "body": "`try runtime.sleep(.fromSeconds(5))` calls `Runtime.sleep` at `src/runtime.zig:1872`, which its own doc comment marks as deprecated in favour of `zio.sleep()`.
